questions.question: Which command is used to create a new virtual environment named 'my_env' using the built-in venv module?
questions.explanation: The standard way to create an environment is using the `-m` (module) flag followed by `venv` and then your chosen folder name.

questions.question: After creating a virtual environment folder, what must you do before you can start installing isolated packages into it?
options: Move the folder to the Desktop
Activate the environment using the specific command for your OS
Nothing, it is automatically active once created
questions.explanation: Creating the folder only sets up the files. You must 'activate' it so your terminal knows to use that specific Python interpreter instead of the system-wide one.

questions.question: How can you tell, just by looking at your terminal/command prompt, that a virtual environment is currently active?
options: The terminal text will turn green
A new window will pop up
The name of the environment (e.g., '.venv') will appear in parentheses at the start of the prompt
Your computer will make a notification sound
questions.explanation: When an environment is active, most terminals will prepend the name of the environment in parentheses, like `(.venv) C:\Users...`, to signify you are in an isolated space.
